Two concurrent oral anticoagulants (with clopidogrel as well) in a 65-year-old with paroxysmal atrial fibrillation/flutter and CLL is a major bleeding hazard; rivaroxaban should have been stopped. Needs urgent reconciliation.

Both 12-lead ECGs recorded that same day (107914094 at 17:13 and 103088543 at 19:36) show an irregularly irregular ventricular response with no discernible P waves at about 139 and 144 bpm - atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response, not sinus rhythm at 72. The documented rhythm and rate are contradicted by the same-day tracings; this matters because the patient is on warfarin for pulmonary embolism and newly documented AF would change management.

Regular narrow-complex rhythm at 69 bpm with a low-amplitude atrial deflection before each QRS and a constant PR of about 165 ms - sinus rhythm (the P wave is small and relatively flat in the inferior leads). Sinus rhythm at 97 bpm with an upright P wave in II/aVF and PR about 118 ms. QRS 72 ms, no bundle branch block; frontal axis about +5 degrees. QT about 306 ms, Bazett QTc about 390 ms. No pacing spikes are present. Only ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison.

Irregularly irregular rhythm with RR intervals ranging 0.69-1.16 s and a completely flat atrial baseline with no P waves in any lead: atrial fibrillation with a slow ventricular response, average rate about 53 bpm. Normal sinus rhythm at 83 bpm, PR about 143 ms, QRS 74 ms, frontal axis about +53 degrees, no bundle branch block. QT about 347 ms, Bazett QTc about 409 ms. Only ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison.

Regular rhythm at 121 bpm with a discrete upright P wave in II preceding each QRS (PR about 182 ms): sinus tachycardia. QRS 92 ms, no bundle branch block; frontal axis about +53 degrees. Normal sinus rhythm at 74 bpm, PR about 182 ms (upper normal, not block), QRS 90 ms, frontal axis about +57 degrees, no bundle branch block. QT about 386 ms, Bazett QTc about 429 ms. Only ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison.

Sinus rhythm at 61 bpm with an upright P wave in I and II before each conducted beat and a PR of about 200 ms (upper limit of normal). QRS 98 ms with no bundle branch block; frontal axis about -31 degrees (left axis deviation). QT about 397 ms, Bazett QTc about 401 ms. Only ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison.

Regular rhythm at 69 bpm with a consistent atrial deflection before each QRS and a PR of about 140 ms - sinus rhythm. QRS 92 ms with no bundle branch block. The frontal plane QRS is almost entirely negative in lead I and in II with a computed axis of about -173 degrees, i.e. an extreme (north-west) axis; with normal precordial R wave progression this pattern raises the possibility of left/right arm lead reversal and should be confirmed on a repeat tracing. QT about 359 ms, Bazett QTc about 386 ms - normal on escitalopram. Only ECG in the chart.

Sinus rhythm at 70 bpm, PR about 152 ms, QRS 94 ms, frontal axis about +35 degrees, no bundle branch block. The T waves are broad and late, giving a QT of about 507 ms and a Bazett QTc of about 548 ms - marked QT prolongation. The previous ECG of 6/17/2020 had a QTc of about 448 ms, so the QTc has increased by more than 60 ms. The patient is on citalopram 40 mg daily; flagged separately for QT safety review.

Sinus rhythm at 68 bpm with an upright P wave in II/aVF and PR about 150 ms. QRS 104 ms - mild non-specific intraventricular conduction delay but no bundle branch block pattern. Frontal axis about +43 degrees. There is lateral/inferior ST depression with T wave inversion in I and aVL; QT about 400 ms with a Bazett QTc of about 440 ms, below the 500 ms review threshold for his escitalopram. Only ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison; the ischaemic-looking repolarisation changes deserve clinical correlation.

Sinus bradycardia at 53 bpm, PR about 172 ms, QRS 90 ms, frontal axis about -5 degrees, no bundle branch block. QT about 394 ms, Bazett QTc about 369 ms. The previous ECG of 12/13/2018 was sinus at 66 bpm with a PR of about 202 ms and QTc about 390 ms; the PR has shortened out of the first degree block range and there is no change in rhythm, bundle branch conduction or QTc.

Sinus rhythm at 68 bpm, PR about 126 ms, QRS 88 ms, frontal axis about +46 degrees, no bundle branch block. The previous ECG of 11/23/2022 had a QTc of about 357 ms, so the QTc has increased by well over 60 ms. This degree of prolongation on escitalopram is clinically significant and is flagged separately for prescriber review; the 5/14/2024 note describing this tracing as having an acceptable QT is not supported.

Regular narrow-complex tachycardia at 141 bpm with an organised upright P wave in II and aVF before each QRS at a 1:1 ratio and PR about 130 ms - sinus tachycardia, not flutter (no sawtooth, and the atrial rate equals the ventricular rate). QRS 84 ms, no bundle branch block; frontal axis about +1 degree. QT about 272 ms, Bazett QTc about 417 ms. The previous ECG of 7/11/2022 showed irregularly irregular atrial fibrillation at about 110 bpm with no P waves, so atrial fibrillation has resolved; QTc change is under 60 ms. No pacing spikes are seen despite the pacemaker in situ.

Normal sinus rhythm at 82 bpm, PR about 160 ms, QRS 102 ms (no bundle branch block pattern), frontal axis about +34 degrees. QT about 382 ms, Bazett QTc about 447 ms. Only ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison.

Sinus rhythm at 91 bpm with an upright P wave in II and PR about 165 ms. QRS 82 ms, no bundle branch block; frontal axis about -15 degrees. QT about 336 ms, Bazett QTc about 413 ms. Sinus tachycardia at 102 bpm, PR about 136 ms, QRS 88 ms, frontal axis about +45 degrees, no bundle branch block. QT about 332 ms, Bazett QTc about 433 ms. The previous ECG the day before (3/18/2025) was essentially identical (sinus 102 bpm, QTc about 437 ms) - no change.

Normal sinus rhythm at 66 bpm, PR about 153 ms, QRS 92 ms, frontal axis about -19 degrees, no bundle branch block. QT about 374 ms, Bazett QTc about 392 ms. Only ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison.

Normal sinus rhythm at 83 bpm, PR about 143 ms, QRS 74 ms, frontal axis about +53 degrees, no bundle branch block. QT about 347 ms, Bazett QTc about 409 ms. Only ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison.

Sinus rhythm at 77 bpm with an upright P wave in II and PR about 150 ms. QRS 70 ms, no bundle branch block; frontal axis about +65 degrees. QT about 397 ms, Bazett QTc about 449 ms. Regular rhythm at 121 bpm with a discrete upright P wave in II preceding each QRS (PR about 182 ms): sinus tachycardia. QRS 92 ms, no bundle branch block; frontal axis about +53 degrees. Sinus bradycardia at 54 bpm. Every QRS is preceded by an upright P wave in II/aVF, but the PR interval is prolonged at about 215 ms - first degree atrioventricular block. Irregularly irregular narrow-complex tachycardia at about 153 bpm (RR 0.29-0.58 s) with a fibrillatory baseline and no organised P waves: atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response. Normal sinus rhythm at 74 bpm, PR about 182 ms (upper normal, not block), QRS 90 ms, frontal axis about +57 degrees, no bundle branch block. QT about 386 ms, Bazett QTc about 429 ms. Only ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison.

The previous ECG of 4/27/2025 was also sinus at 60 bpm with QTc about 404 ms; its markedly negative lead I suggests limb-lead reversal on that study. No change in rhythm, conduction or QTc.

Sinus rhythm at 97 bpm with an upright P wave in II/aVF and PR about 118 ms. QRS 72 ms, no bundle branch block; frontal axis about +5 degrees. QT about 306 ms, Bazett QTc about 390 ms. No pacing spikes are present. Only ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison.

Normal sinus rhythm at 72 bpm, PR about 138 ms, QRS 82 ms, frontal axis about +22 degrees, no bundle branch block. QT about 366 ms, Bazett QTc about 401 ms - normal. Only ECG in the chart; note that this tracing predates the escitalopram started 8/1/2026, for which a follow-up ECG is outstanding.

Irregularly irregular rhythm with RR intervals ranging 0.69-1.16 s and a completely flat atrial baseline with no P waves in any lead: atrial fibrillation with a slow ventricular response, average rate about 53 bpm. No measurable PR interval. QRS 92 ms, no bundle branch block; frontal axis about +15 degrees. QT about 433 ms, Bazett QTc about 408 ms. The previous ECG three days earlier (11/12/2024) showed sinus rhythm at 69 bpm with a clear P wave and PR about 178 ms, so atrial fibrillation is new; QTc is essentially unchanged.

Sinus bradycardia at 58 bpm with upright P waves in II and PR about 106 ms. QRS 88 ms, no bundle branch block; frontal axis about +61 degrees. QT about 420 ms, Bazett QTc about 414 ms. The previous tracing one day earlier was also sinus at 62 bpm with QTc about 448 ms - no change in rhythm or conduction and QTc change under 60 ms. No pacing spikes.

Normal sinus rhythm at 83 bpm, PR about 143 ms, QRS 74 ms, frontal axis about +53 degrees, no bundle branch block. QT about 347 ms, Bazett QTc about 409 ms. Only ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison.

Sinus rhythm at 77 bpm with an upright P wave in II and PR about 150 ms. QRS 70 ms, no bundle branch block; frontal axis about +65 degrees. QT about 397 ms, Bazett QTc about 449 ms. The previous ECG of 2/2/2020 was sinus with frequent premature beats and a QTc of about 523 ms; the QTc has fallen by more than 60 ms on this tracing.

Regular rhythm at 121 bpm with a discrete upright P wave in II preceding each QRS (PR about 182 ms): sinus tachycardia. QRS 92 ms, no bundle branch block; frontal axis about +53 degrees. QT about 275 ms, QTc (Bazett) about 390 ms. Compared with the previous tracing of 9/16/2016 (sinus tachycardia 108 bpm, QTc about 400 ms) there is no change in rhythm, conduction or QTc (change less than 60 ms).

Sinus bradycardia at 54 bpm. Every QRS is preceded by an upright P wave in II/aVF, but the PR interval is prolonged at about 215 ms - first degree atrioventricular block. QRS 86 ms with a prominent R wave in V1 but no bundle branch block pattern; frontal axis about +4 degrees. QT about 401 ms, Bazett QTc about 381 ms. The prior ECG of 11/30/2024 was sinus at 51 bpm with PR about 188 ms and QTc about 364 ms - no change in rhythm, no new bundle branch block and QTc change under 60 ms.

Irregularly irregular narrow-complex tachycardia at about 153 bpm (RR 0.29-0.58 s) with a fibrillatory baseline and no organised P waves: atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response. The previous ECG the evening before (9/12/2025) showed sinus rhythm at 77 bpm with a P wave and PR about 148 ms, so atrial fibrillation is new; QTc is unchanged.

Sinus rhythm at 73 bpm with upright P waves in II and PR about 170 ms. QRS 88 ms, no bundle branch block; frontal axis about +13 degrees. QT about 360 ms, Bazett QTc about 398 ms - normal. Normal sinus rhythm at 74 bpm, PR about 182 ms (upper normal, not block), QRS 90 ms, frontal axis about +57 degrees, no bundle branch block. QT about 386 ms, Bazett QTc about 429 ms. Only ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison.

Sinus tachycardia at 112 bpm with a clear upright P wave in II before every QRS and PR about 162 ms - no flutter waves despite the history of atrial flutter. QRS 90 ms, no bundle branch block; frontal axis about +35 degrees. Very deep S waves in V1-V2 with tall lateral R waves suggest left ventricular hypertrophy. QT about 289 ms, Bazett QTc about 394 ms. The prior ECG of 7/4/2022 was virtually identical (sinus 115 bpm, QTc about 390 ms) - no change.

Sinus rhythm at 61 bpm with an upright P wave in I and II before each conducted beat and a PR of about 200 ms (upper limit of normal). One early wide complex with a compensatory pause is a premature ventricular beat; the underlying rhythm is sinus. QRS 98 ms with no bundle branch block; frontal axis about -31 degrees (left axis deviation). QT about 397 ms, Bazett QTc about 401 ms. Only ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison.

Regular rhythm at 69 bpm with a consistent atrial deflection before each QRS and a PR of about 140 ms - sinus rhythm. QRS 92 ms with no bundle branch block. The frontal plane QRS is almost entirely negative in lead I and in II with a computed axis of about -173 degrees, i.e. an extreme (north-west) axis; with normal precordial R wave progression this pattern raises the possibility of left/right arm lead reversal and should be confirmed on a repeat tracing. QT about 359 ms, Bazett QTc about 386 ms - normal on escitalopram. Only ECG in the chart.

Sinus rhythm at 70 bpm, PR about 152 ms, QRS 94 ms, frontal axis about +35 degrees, no bundle branch block. The T waves are broad and late, giving a QT of about 507 ms and a Bazett QTc of about 548 ms - marked QT prolongation. The previous ECG of 6/17/2020 had a QTc of about 448 ms, so the QTc has increased by more than 60 ms. The patient is on citalopram 40 mg daily; flagged separately for QT safety review.

Sinus rhythm at 68 bpm with an upright P wave in II/aVF and PR about 150 ms. QRS 104 ms - mild non-specific intraventricular conduction delay but no bundle branch block pattern. Frontal axis about +43 degrees. There is lateral/inferior ST depression with T wave inversion in I and aVL; QT about 400 ms with a Bazett QTc of about 440 ms, below the 500 ms review threshold for his escitalopram. Only ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison; the ischaemic-looking repolarisation changes deserve clinical correlation.

Sinus bradycardia at 53 bpm, PR about 172 ms, QRS 90 ms, frontal axis about -5 degrees, no bundle branch block. QT about 394 ms, Bazett QTc about 369 ms. The previous ECG of 12/13/2018 was sinus at 66 bpm with a PR of about 202 ms and QTc about 390 ms; the PR has shortened out of the first degree block range and there is no change in rhythm, bundle branch conduction or QTc.

Sinus rhythm at 68 bpm, PR about 126 ms, QRS 88 ms, frontal axis about +46 degrees, no bundle branch block. The T waves are broad and the QT is markedly long: QT about 493 ms giving a Bazett QTc of about 526 ms. The previous ECG of 11/23/2022 had a QTc of about 357 ms, so the QTc has increased by well over 60 ms. This degree of prolongation on escitalopram is clinically significant and is flagged separately for prescriber review; the 5/14/2024 note describing this tracing as having an acceptable QT is not supported.

Regular narrow-complex tachycardia at 141 bpm with an organised upright P wave in II and aVF before each QRS at a 1:1 ratio and PR about 130 ms - sinus tachycardia, not flutter (no sawtooth, and the atrial rate equals the ventricular rate). QRS 84 ms, no bundle branch block; frontal axis about +1 degree. QT about 272 ms, Bazett QTc about 417 ms. The previous ECG of 7/11/2022 showed irregularly irregular atrial fibrillation at about 110 bpm with no P waves, so atrial fibrillation has resolved; QTc change is under 60 ms. No pacing spikes are seen despite the pacemaker in situ.

Normal sinus rhythm at 82 bpm, PR about 160 ms, QRS 102 ms (no bundle branch block pattern), frontal axis about +34 degrees. QT about 382 ms, Bazett QTc about 447 ms. Only ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison.

Sinus rhythm at 91 bpm with an upright P wave in II and PR about 165 ms. QRS 82 ms, no bundle branch block; frontal axis about -15 degrees. QT about 336 ms, Bazett QTc about 413 ms. The previous ECG of 5/16/2021 was sinus at 87 bpm with QTc about 397 ms - no change in rhythm, conduction or QTc. No pacing spikes are present.

Sinus rhythm at 61 bpm with an upright P wave in II before each QRS but a prolonged PR of about 215 ms - first degree atrioventricular block. The QRS is wide at 132 ms with a broad monophasic R wave in I, aVL and V6 and deep QS/rS complexes in V1-V3: left bundle branch block. Frontal axis about -21 degrees (normal). QT about 438 ms, Bazett QTc about 442 ms (secondary repolarisation change from the LBBB). The previous ECG of 6/3/2024 already showed the same left bundle branch block (QRS about 130 ms) with PR about 216 ms and QTc about 450 ms, so there is no new conduction abnormality and no significant QTc change.

Sinus tachycardia at 102 bpm, PR about 136 ms, QRS 88 ms, frontal axis about +45 degrees, no bundle branch block. QT about 332 ms, Bazett QTc about 433 ms. The previous ECG the day before (3/18/2025) was essentially identical (sinus 102 bpm, QTc about 437 ms) - no change.

Normal sinus rhythm at 66 bpm, PR about 153 ms, QRS 92 ms, frontal axis about -19 degrees, no bundle branch block. QT about 374 ms, Bazett QTc about 392 ms. Only ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison.

Sinus bradycardia at 58 bpm with an upright P wave in II before each QRS and a PR of about 198 ms (upper limit of normal). QRS 86 ms, no bundle branch block; frontal axis about +36 degrees. The T waves are very broad: QT about 589 ms with a Bazett QTc of about 577 ms - marked QT prolongation on amiodarone. The previous ECG of 4/6/2022 showed irregularly irregular atrial fibrillation at about 131 bpm with a QTc of about 443 ms, so atrial fibrillation has resolved (sinus rhythm restored) and the QTc has increased by more than 60 ms. Flagged separately for QT safety review.

Sinus tachycardia at 121 bpm with an upright P wave in II before each QRS and PR about 130 ms. QRS 78 ms, no bundle branch block; frontal axis about +69 degrees (normal). QT about 288 ms, Bazett QTc about 409 ms. Only ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison.

Sinus rhythm at 101 bpm, PR about 144 ms, QRS 88 ms, frontal axis about +58 degrees, no conduction block. Deep S in V1 with tall R in V5/V6 but QRS duration normal. QT about 321 ms, QTc about 417 ms. The immediately preceding tracing the same morning (102910502, 10:06) was identical (sinus 101 bpm, QTc about 409 ms) - no interval change.

Sinus bradycardia at 52 bpm with an upright P in II and PR about 164 ms. QRS 94 ms with no bundle branch block; frontal axis about +36 degrees. Voltage is high (R in V5 about 4 mV) suggesting left ventricular hypertrophy. QT about 417 ms, QTc about 387 ms. Compared with 5/22/2023 (sinus 58 bpm with an isolated premature beat, QTc about 349 ms) there is no change in rhythm or conduction and the QTc change is under 60 ms.

Sinus tachycardia at 122 bpm, PR about 136 ms, QRS now narrow at 90 ms. The frontal axis is about +140 degrees (right axis deviation) with a dominant S wave in I, V5 and V6. QT about 290 ms, QTc about 413 ms. The earlier tracing the same day (106516875, 01:33) showed a wide QRS of about 150 ms with a terminal R prime in V1 and wide terminal S waves in I and V6, i.e. right bundle branch block; that pattern has disappeared on this tracing, so the bundle branch block has resolved (rate-related aberrancy). QTc change (about -46 ms) is less than 60 ms.

Sinus rhythm at 62 bpm with upright P waves in II/aVF and PR about 166 ms. QRS 98 ms, no bundle branch block; frontal axis about +67 degrees. The T waves are strikingly broad and prolonged: QT about 548 ms with a Bazett QTc of about 557 ms - marked QT prolongation. The previous ECG (6/7/2025) had a QTc of about 416 ms, an increase of well over 60 ms, in keeping with amiodarone started 11/10/2025. Flagged separately for QT safety review.

Irregularly irregular narrow-complex rhythm with RR intervals from 0.39 to 1.09 s and no discernible P waves on any lead (flat, low-amplitude baseline between QRS complexes): atrial fibrillation with an average ventricular rate of about 99 bpm. No measurable PR interval. QRS 78 ms with no bundle branch block; frontal axis about -50 degrees (left axis deviation). QT about 328 ms, Bazett QTc about 415 ms. Only ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison.

QT about 327 ms, Bazett QTc about 437 ms. The previous ECG of 7/27/2019 was sinus at 75 bpm with QTc about 434 ms - no change in rhythm, conduction or QTc.

items.explanation: 80-year-old woman with persistent atrial fibrillation documented in every cardiology clinic note from 9/12/2025 through 6/22/2026. Current medications (note of 6/22/2026 and active orders) are aspirin 81 mg and gabapentin only - no oral anticoagulant is ordered or active as of 2026-09-24. CHA2DS2-VASc = 9 (CHF: hypertensive heart disease with heart failure / acute on chronic combined systolic and diastolic heart failure; hypertension; age 80 = 2; type 2 diabetes mellitus; prior cerebral infarction with residual hemiplegia and dysarthria = 2; vascular disease: atherosclerotic coronary disease and old myocardial infarction; female). Guideline-directed oral anticoagulation is indicated (Class 1); aspirin alone is not adequate stroke prophylaxis. Needs prescriber review for initiation of anticoagulation.

35-year-old woman on citalopram 40 mg daily (current order 7/15/2026 to 1/7/2027; 40 mg also exceeds the 20 mg maximum recommended where QT prolongation is a concern). Her most recent ECG (104821039, 11/10/2023) shows sinus rhythm at 70 bpm with QT about 507 ms and Bazett QTc about 548 ms, above the 500 ms review threshold and much longer than her 2020 tracing (QTc about 448 ms). Potassium 4.6 mmol/L (7/15/2026) and magnesium 2.0 mg/dL (3/8/2025) are normal. Prescriber review of the citalopram dose and a repeat ECG are required.

95-year-old woman on amiodarone 200 mg daily (current order 6/17/2026 to 1/6/2027, a QT watch-list drug taken continuously since 2022). Her most recent ECG (101515306, 4/27/2022) shows sinus rhythm at 58 bpm with QT about 589 ms and Bazett QTc about 577 ms, far above the 500 ms threshold. Most recent potassium 4.2 mmol/L and magnesium 1.9 mg/dL (6/17/2026) are normal. She is also on warfarin and a beta blocker; prescriber review of continued amiodarone and an up-to-date ECG are required.

Amiodarone 200 mg daily (QT watch-list) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 11/10/2025; it does not appear in any earlier outpatient medication list. Because the start was on or after 9/1/2025 and before 3/1/2026, the 9/1/2025 memo applies and an ECG was due within 30 days, i.e. by 12/10/2025. ECG 106885519 was recorded on 11/24/2025, 14 days after the start, so the monitoring requirement was met. (That ECG shows QTc about 557 ms - see the separate QT safety item.)

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch-list) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2/12/2026 and has been continued since. The start was on or after 9/1/2025 and before 3/1/2026, so the 9/1/2025 memo applies (30-day window), making the ECG due by 3/14/2026. ECG 101538691 was obtained on 3/8/2026, 24 days after the start, so the requirement was met. That tracing shows sinus rhythm at 68 bpm with QTc about 420 ms, below the 500 ms review threshold.

Citalopram 40 mg daily (QT watch-list) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 3/2/2026. Because the start was on or after 3/1/2026 the revised memo applies and an ECG was due within 14 days, i.e. by 3/16/2026. ECG 104882441 was recorded at the 3/7/2026 clinic visit, 5 days after the start, so the requirement was met; it shows sinus rhythm at 81 bpm with QTc about 378 ms.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch-list) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 4/10/2026 and has been refilled since. The start is after 3/1/2026, so the revised memo applies and an ECG was due within 14 days, by 4/24/2026. The only ECG in the chart (107859369) was not recorded until 4/29/2026, 19 days after the start - outside the required window, so the requirement was not met on time and is overdue. The late tracing was reassuring (sinus rhythm 69 bpm, QTc about 386 ms), but the monitoring lapse should be reviewed.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch-list) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 8/1/2026 (it was not on the medication list at the previous clinic visit of 2/18/2026; the only prior exposure was a brief inpatient course in December 2025). The start is after 3/1/2026, so an ECG was required within 14 days, by 8/15/2026. No ECG has been obtained since 12/25/2025, so the requirement is overdue as of 2026-09-24.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch-list) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 8/10/2026 (not on the medication list at the 3/8/2026 visit). The start is after 3/1/2026, so an ECG was required within 14 days, by 8/24/2026. The nurse note of 8/25/2026 records that the patient had an ECG at Northside Urgent Care on 8/18/2026 - within the window - but the report was requested by fax and has not been received, and no tracing for this patient exists in the chart. The requirement may already have been met by that outside study, so completion cannot be determined until the report is obtained.

Haloperidol 2 mg twice daily (QT watch-list) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 9/15/2026. Under the revised 3/1/2026 memo an ECG is required within 14 days of the start, i.e. by 9/29/2026. No ECG has been obtained since 3/9/2025, but the window has not yet closed as of the evaluation time of 2026-09-24, so the requirement is not yet due. It should be tracked to ensure the ECG is done.

At the Cardiology Clinic visit of 9/1/2026 Dr. Kessler documented INR 1.6, subtherapeutic, and increased warfarin from 5 mg to 7.5 mg daily. Under the 3/1/2026 memo an INR is required within 7 days of a dose change made by a clinic clinician, i.e. by 9/8/2026. INR 2.3 was resulted on 9/5/2026, 4 days later, so the requirement was met.

48-year-old man with atrial fibrillation (paroxysmal atrial fibrillation / atrial fibrillation on the problem list, also cited in every cardiology clinic note). Current medications at the last visit (8/4/2026) and active orders are famotidine, pantoprazole and sertraline - no anticoagulant is current as of 2026-09-24, despite a chart history of long-term anticoagulant use. CHA2DS2-VASc = 2 (congestive heart failure / acute systolic heart failure and non-ischaemic cardiomyopathy; essential hypertension with hypertensive chronic kidney disease). A score of 2 in a man meets the 2023 ACC/AHA/ACCP/HRS Class 1 recommendation for oral anticoagulation. Needs prescriber review.

Anticoagulation clinic telephone note of 9/10/2026 by L. Nguyen, PharmD: home INR 3.4, warfarin decreased from 5 mg to 4 mg daily per protocol. A clinic pharmacist adjusting warfarin under the standing order is covered by the 3/1/2026 memo, so an INR was required within 7 days, by 9/17/2026. The last INR in the chart is 2.7 from 6/17/2026; no INR has been drawn since the dose change, so the follow-up is overdue as of 2026-09-24 in a 95-year-old who was supratherapeutic.

71-year-old woman with paroxysmal atrial fibrillation on the problem list. Current medications at the most recent visit (6/23/2026) and active orders are famotidine, levothyroxine and metoprolol tartrate - rate control only, with no anticoagulant current as of 2026-09-24. CHA2DS2-VASc = 5 (hypertension; age 71 = 1; prior cerebral infarction/embolic stroke with residual hemiplegia and ataxia = 2; female). Oral anticoagulation is strongly indicated for secondary stroke prevention. Needs prescriber review.

71-year-old man with atrial fibrillation on the problem list, cited in each cardiology clinic note. The most recent visit (6/27/2026) lists levothyroxine only, and the only active outpatient order as of 2026-09-24 is levothyroxine - no anticoagulant. CHA2DS2-VASc = 3 (essential hypertension; age 71 = 1; vascular disease - coronary atherosclerosis of a native coronary artery). Anticoagulation is recommended (Class 1). Prior documented hemorrhage complicating a procedure should be weighed, but the gap in therapy needs prescriber review.

Outside records reviewed 8/12/2026 document an admission 8/2-8/5/2026 for upper GI bleeding from a duodenal ulcer (haemoglobin nadir 6.9, 2 units transfused) with apixaban HELD at discharge pending cardiology review. At the cardiology visit of 8/20/2026 apixaban 5 mg twice daily was nevertheless re-ordered (valid 2026-08-20 to 2027-01-04) and remains current on 2026-09-24, alongside aspirin and clopidogrel, with no documented decision that the bleeding risk had been reconsidered. Anticoagulation plus dual antiplatelet therapy after a recent major GI bleed requires prescriber review before it continues.

At the cardiology visit of 7/15/2026 the plan was to switch the anticoagulant from rivaroxaban to apixaban for insurance coverage, but both drugs were ordered the same day and both remain current on 2026-09-24: apixaban 5 mg twice daily (2026-07-15 to 2026-12-23) and rivaroxaban 20 mg daily (2026-07-15 to 2027-01-03). The visit note itself lists both agents in the current medication list. Two concurrent oral anticoagulants (with clopidogrel as well) in a 65-year-old with paroxysmal atrial fibrillation/flutter and CLL is a major bleeding hazard; rivaroxaban should have been stopped. Needs urgent reconciliation.

The cardiology clinic note of 6/10/2026 states "ECG obtained today: normal sinus rhythm, rate 72". Both 12-lead ECGs recorded that same day (107914094 at 17:13 and 103088543 at 19:36) show an irregularly irregular ventricular response with no discernible P waves at about 139 and 144 bpm - atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response, not sinus rhythm at 72. The documented rhythm and rate are contradicted by the same-day tracings; this matters because the patient is on warfarin for pulmonary embolism and newly documented AF would change management.

79-year-old man on amiodarone 200 mg daily (current order 7/12/2026 to 1/9/2027, a QT watch-list drug). His most recent ECG (106885519, 11/24/2025) shows sinus rhythm at 62 bpm with QT about 548 ms and Bazett QTc about 557 ms, well above the 500 ms threshold in the QT monitoring memo of 1/15/2025. Most recent electrolytes are normal (K 4.3 mmol/L and Mg 2.1 mg/dL on 6/9/2026), so the prolongation is drug/substrate related. Prescriber review of amiodarone and repeat ECG are required.

56-year-old man on escitalopram 10 mg daily (current order 7/18/2026 to 12/26/2026, a QT watch-list drug, continuously prescribed since 5/14/2024). His most recent ECG (108018814, 10/8/2023 - the tracing the 5/14/2024 note described as having an acceptable QT) actually shows sinus rhythm at 68 bpm with QT about 493 ms and Bazett QTc about 526 ms, i.e. 500 ms or more, and markedly longer than the prior tracing (QTc about 357 ms on 11/23/2022). Potassium 3.8 mmol/L and magnesium 1.9 mg/dL (3/18/2026) are acceptable. Prescriber review and a current ECG are required.

CHA2DS2-VASc = 3 (essential hypertension; age 71 = 1; vascular disease - coronary atherosclerosis of a native coronary artery). Anticoagulation is recommended (Class 1). Prior documented hemorrhage complicating a procedure should be weighed, but the gap in therapy needs prescriber review.

Two concurrent oral anticoagulants (with clopidogrel as well) in a 65-year-old with paroxysmal atrial fibrillation/flutter and CLL is a major bleeding hazard; rivaroxaban should have been stopped. Needs urgent reconciliation.

items.explanation: 80-year-old woman with persistent atrial fibrillation documented in every cardiology clinic note from 9/12/2025 through 6/22/2026. Current medications (note of 6/22/2026 and active orders) are aspirin 81 mg and gabapentin only - no oral anticoagulant is ordered or active as of 2026-09-24. CHA2DS2-VASc = 9 (CHF: hypertensive heart disease with heart failure / acute on chronic combined systolic and diastolic heart failure; hypertension; age 80 = 2; type 2 diabetes mellitus; prior cerebral infarction with residual hemiplegia and dysarthria = 2; vascular disease: atherosclerotic coronary disease and old myocardial infarction; female). Guideline-directed oral anticoagulation is indicated (Class 1); aspirin alone is not adequate stroke prophylaxis. Needs prescriber review for initiation of anticoagulation.

35-year-old woman on citalopram 40 mg daily (current order 7/15/2026 to 1/7/2027; 40 mg also exceeds the 20 mg maximum recommended where QT prolongation is a concern). Her most recent ECG (104821039, 11/10/2023) shows sinus rhythm at 70 bpm with QT about 507 ms and Bazett QTc about 548 ms, above the 500 ms review threshold and much longer than her 2020 tracing (QTc about 448 ms). Potassium 4.6 mmol/L (7/15/2026) and magnesium 2.0 mg/dL (3/8/2025) are normal. Prescriber review of the citalopram dose and a repeat ECG are required.

95-year-old woman on amiodarone 200 mg daily (current order 6/17/2026 to 1/6/2027, a QT watch-list drug taken continuously since 2022). Her most recent ECG (101515306, 4/27/2022) shows sinus rhythm at 58 bpm with QT about 589 ms and Bazett QTc about 577 ms, far above the 500 ms threshold. Most recent potassium 4.2 mmol/L and magnesium 1.9 mg/dL (6/17/2026) are normal. She is also on warfarin and a beta blocker; prescriber review of continued amiodarone and an up-to-date ECG are required.

Amiodarone 200 mg daily (QT watch-list) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 11/10/2025; it does not appear in any earlier outpatient medication list. Because the start was on or after 9/1/2025 and before 3/1/2026, the 9/1/2025 memo applies and an ECG was due within 30 days, i.e. by 12/10/2025. ECG 106885519 was recorded on 11/24/2025, 14 days after the start, so the monitoring requirement was met. (That ECG shows QTc about 557 ms - see the separate QT safety item.)

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch-list) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2/12/2026 and has been continued since. The start was on or after 9/1/2025 and before 3/1/2026, so the 9/1/2025 memo applies (30-day window), making the ECG due by 3/14/2026. ECG 101538691 was obtained on 3/8/2026, 24 days after the start, so the requirement was met. That tracing shows sinus rhythm at 68 bpm with QTc about 420 ms, below the 500 ms review threshold.

Citalopram 40 mg daily (QT watch-list) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 3/2/2026. Because the start was on or after 3/1/2026 the revised memo applies and an ECG was due within 14 days, i.e. by 3/16/2026. ECG 104882441 was recorded at the 3/7/2026 clinic visit, 5 days after the start, so the requirement was met; it shows sinus rhythm at 81 bpm with QTc about 378 ms.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch-list) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 4/10/2026 and has been refilled since. The start is after 3/1/2026, so the revised memo applies and an ECG was due within 14 days, by 4/24/2026. The only ECG in the chart (107859369) was not recorded until 4/29/2026, 19 days after the start - outside the required window, so the requirement was not met on time and is overdue. The late tracing was reassuring (sinus rhythm 69 bpm, QTc about 386 ms), but the monitoring lapse should be reviewed.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch-list) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 8/1/2026 (it was not on the medication list at the previous clinic visit of 2/18/2026; the only prior exposure was a brief inpatient course in December 2025). The start is after 3/1/2026, so an ECG was required within 14 days, by 8/15/2026. No ECG has been obtained since 12/25/2025, so the requirement is overdue as of 2026-09-24.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch-list) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 8/10/2026 (not on the medication list at the 3/8/2026 visit). The requirement may already have been met by that outside study, so completion cannot be determined until the report is obtained.

Haloperidol 2 mg twice daily (QT watch-list) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 9/15/2026. Under the revised 3/1/2026 memo an ECG is required within 14 days of the start, i.e. by 9/29/2026. No ECG has been obtained since 3/9/2025, but the window has not yet closed as of the evaluation time of 2026-09-24, so the requirement is not yet due. It should be tracked to ensure the ECG is done.

Under the 3/1/2026 memo an INR is required within 7 days of a dose change made by a clinic clinician, i.e. by 9/8/2026. INR 2.3 was resulted on 9/5/2026, 4 days later, so the requirement was met.

48-year-old man with atrial fibrillation (paroxysmal atrial fibrillation / atrial fibrillation on the problem list, also cited in every cardiology clinic note). Current medications at the last visit (8/4/2026) and active orders are famotidine, pantoprazole and sertraline - no anticoagulant is current as of 2026-09-24, despite a chart history of long-term anticoagulant use. CHA2DS2-VASc = 2 (congestive heart failure / acute systolic heart failure and non-ischaemic cardiomyopathy; essential hypertension with hypertensive chronic kidney disease). A score of 2 in a man meets the 2023 ACC/AHA/ACCP/HRS Class 1 recommendation for oral anticoagulation. Needs prescriber review.

The last INR in the chart is 2.7 from 6/17/2026; no INR has been drawn since the dose change, so the follow-up is overdue as of 2026-09-24 in a 95-year-old who was supratherapeutic.

CHA2DS2-VASc = 5 (hypertension; age 71 = 1; prior cerebral infarction/embolic stroke with residual hemiplegia and ataxia = 2; female). Oral anticoagulation is strongly indicated for secondary stroke prevention. Needs prescriber review.

CHA2DS2-VASc = 3 (essential hypertension; age 71 = 1; vascular disease - coronary atherosclerosis of a native coronary artery). Anticoagulation is recommended (Class 1). Prior documented hemorrhage complicating a procedure should be weighed, but the gap in therapy needs prescriber review.

Anticoagulation plus dual antiplatelet therapy after a recent major GI bleed requires prescriber review before it continues.

At the cardiology visit of 7/15/2026 the plan was to switch the anticoagulant from rivaroxaban to apixaban for insurance coverage, but both drugs were ordered the same day and both remain current on 2026-09-24: apixaban 5 mg twice daily (2026-07-15 to 2026-12-23) and rivaroxaban 20 mg daily (2026-07-15 to 2027-01-03). The visit note itself lists both agents in the current medication list. Two concurrent oral anticoagulants (with clopidogrel as well) in a 65-year-old with paroxysmal atrial fibrillation/flutter and CLL is a major bleeding hazard; rivaroxaban should have been stopped. Needs urgent reconciliation.

Both 12-lead ECGs recorded that same day (107914094 at 17:13 and 103088543 at 19:36) show an irregularly irregular ventricular response with no discernible P waves at about 139 and 144 bpm - atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response, not sinus rhythm at 72. The documented rhythm and rate are contradicted by the same-day tracings; this matters because the patient is on warfarin for pulmonary embolism and newly documented AF would change management.

items.explanation: 80-year-old woman with persistent atrial fibrillation documented in every cardiology clinic note from 9/12/2025 through 6/22/2026. The visit note itself lists both agents in the current medication list. Two concurrent oral anticoagulants (with clopidogrel as well) in a 65-year-old with paroxysmal atrial fibrillation/flutter and CLL is a major bleeding hazard; rivaroxaban should have been stopped. Needs urgent reconciliation.
